subject: Production: spike in initial-response p99 — upstream TLS/handshake impact
messages:
From: James Li <james@stellarpay.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: tina@stellarpay.com
Date: 2026-08-14T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Severe latency spike affecting checkout (p99 initial-response)

Ben —

We're seeing a serious regression this morning: p95 and p99 for initial-response (time-to-first-token) on the Hosted API for our checkout flow have spiked ~6x starting ~08:40 PDT. This is causing timeouts in our frontend and a significant drop in conversions.

Quick facts:
- Impact window: ~08:40–ongoing (first noticed 09:02 PDT)
- Example request IDs: req_e2f1a3, req_e2f1a4 (attached request id list)
- Symptoms: long stall before first token, then normal throughput after token emitted
- Affected region: us-east primarily

We need an urgent triage and either a mitigation or a rollback. Can you confirm whether this looks like something on Redwood's side or our CDN upstream? Screenshots attached.

Thanks — this is P1 for us.

James Li
Head of Payments, StellarPay
attachments: p99-dashboard-screenshot.png

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: James Li <james@stellarpay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-14T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency spike affecting checkout (p99 initial-response)

James —

Thanks for the heads up and the screenshots. We see the same elevated p95/p99 on our side for calls from your account. I've looped in Marissa (CS) and we'll get engineering on this immediately.

Immediate next steps:
- Internal triage to identify whether this is on Redwood's upstream traffic or the customer CDN path
- Gather connection-level traces and TLS handshake logs (we'll share attachments)
- Short term mitigation options (routing/POP failover, session-ticket tuning)

I'll update you within 30 minutes with our initial findings. Sorry for the disruption — we're treating this as a priority.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-14T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Severe latency spike affecting checkout (p99 initial-response) — initial findings

Quick summary of findings from us-east POPs (initial 20 minutes):
- Observed large increase in TLS full-handshake occurrences (no session resumption) for connections originating from StellarPay's IP ranges.
- Handshake durations: median ~40ms -> spike to 350–900ms on tail; matches the customer's TTFT symptom (stall before first token).
- No increased token-generation time inside model runtime; once connection established, token emission is normal.
- Datadog traces: https://app.datadog.com/dashboard/xxxx/hosted-ttft-spike (link) shows p99 dominated by connect/handshake span.
- Capture: attached handshake-logs.tar.gz (TLS client_hello/server_hello timings, session ticket data).

Likely cause: upstream CDN/origin path between our edge and the customer's CDN is intermittently failing to resume TLS sessions, forcing full handshakes and sometimes triggering retransmit/retry logic that delays the first byte/token. We also saw occasional TCP retransmit bursts on those connections.

Immediate mitigation options (we can action in the next 30–60m):
1) Route StellarPay traffic via an alternate POP (us-east-2) — will drop in new connections gradually; reduces exposure to the problematic upstream path.
2) Enable aggressive TLS session-ticket reuse and increase socket keepalive on connection pool to favor warm connections (low-risk config change on our side).
3) Ask StellarPay to enable session resumption on their CDN/origin (customer-side change) — we can provide exact config snippets.

Longer-term: work with the CDN provider to root-cause packet-level retransmits/renegotiation. Also add a tracing metric for "handshake_count" per client prefix to detect this earlier.

I'll prepare a short mitigation playbook and can run (1) and (2) now if you authorize.

— Rishi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
attachments: handshake-logs.tar.gz

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: James Li <james@stellarpay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency spike affecting checkout (p99 initial-response) — mitigation plan and next steps

James —

Thank you for the patience. Engineering (Rishi) found that the primary symptom is extended TLS full-handshakes between our edge and your CDN/origin, which is increasing initial-response p99. This is not a model runtime issue — it's connection-level.

Our proposed immediate actions (we can run these now):
- Short-term (we will do): 1) Route your traffic to an alternate us-east POP to avoid the problematic upstream path, 2) enable TLS session-ticket reuse + increase connection keepalives on our side to favor warm connections. These changes are low-risk and reversible.
- Customer action requested: please enable TLS session resumption on your CDN/origin and confirm session-ticket acceptance; we will provide exact config guidance.

We will also provide a credit for impacted calls for the window of 08:40–when we confirm recovery; more details in a follow-up. We expect to have the short-term mitigations deployed within 45 minutes and will update you at 10:30 PDT.

If you can allow a brief maintenance window at ~10:15 PDT for the POP reroute, that will help ensure a controlled change.

Apologies again — we are prioritizing this.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Ben / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. We applied the suggested CDN session-resumption patch at 10:20 PDT and I can confirm p99 for initial-response dropped back to baseline by ~10:28 PDT. The alternate POP + session-ticket changes on your side also helped.

Please proceed with the post-incident credit and send the postmortem when available. We'll keep the ticket open until we see the full RCA and CDN vendor notes.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

James
